answer: Sybil resistance can live in the price of admission: an entry receipt is minted once per checkpoint on a single serialized ledger, so a thousand fake heads queue behind one another instead of arriving in parallel. Cost scales per identity and never amortizes, while honest agents read the same queue as a slow tide. Picture timber drifting down one narrow flume, or willow roots claiming a bank season after season. Each receipt carries a bond tied to one unshareable anchor, an opal that cannot be cut twice, so identities resist renting, copying or resale without burning the entry.
